question: Do deep completions add to xG and market ratings in the soccer game model?
answer: No. Every weight raised 1X2 log loss on 2015-22 (+.02 to +.46 x1000), so it was never taken to the held-out seasons.
findings: The best setting (gain .08, weight .03) was +.02 x1000, t by day .39, better in 4/8 seasons, over 19,466 matches.
At a weight of .10 it was +.19 to +.46 x1000 (t up to 2.29). More weight on deep completions is worse.
Moving .05 of the xG weight to deep was +.21 x1000, t = 1.61. Deep is weaker than xG at the same weight.
In the base model the market ratings carry ~.89 of the blend and xG .11, so a process stat has little room.
method: Deep completions (Understat 'deep', passes completed within ~20 m of goal) are put on the goal scale by one ratio (.234 goals per deep, big five 2015-22) and walked as a fifth side rating like xG. They are scored on 90-minute 1X2 log loss, paired by match, with t from match-day sums. The grid was pre-registered, and held 2023-26 is untouched.
data: ESPN results + football-data closes + Understat team match histories, big five 2015-22 scored with UEFA matches; 21,359 matches with deep counts.
split_check: No setting beat the base in more than 4 of 8 seasons.

chart.title: Log loss change x1000 by setting (tuning)
